summary: Level 1-220 (+ AI title levels 1-30 + LE research) leveling path, hunting spots, bot ladder and key quests for the Engineer (profession 3), written for AOBuddy10. The Engineer levels behind a ROBOT: every bot nano is a Profession(60)==3 nano whose ToUse action requires Matter Creation (stat 130) and Time & Space (stat 131) at (near-)equal values AND a Cash (stat 61) amount, and whose effect is 'Hit[61,-cost,-cost]' (a literal credit drain) plus SpawnItem[<shell>,<PET LEVEL>,0]. That second SpawnItem argument is the bot's LEVEL, which is how the ladder below is derived - every pet level here is read out of nanos.ocp, not guessed. The whole leveling identity is: summon the biggest bot you can control, send it in, shoot/grenade from behind it, repair it with the Pet Heals line, and re-summon when it dies. The signature Engineer trick is running a bot ABOVE your own nano skills using a Trader Wrangle and/or an MP's Mocham's Gift: you only need 80% of the casting requirement to keep the bot obeying you, so a buffed cast leaves you a bot you can still control after the buff drops. This file is a curated aggregation of LOCAL client data (bot ladder, nano ids, item ids, playfield names) plus reputable community sources for the route (see _sources); anything not cleanly cross-checked is in _unverified.

petMechanics.castCost: Every robot nano from 'Feeble Android' (45712) upward also carries a Cash (stat 61) requirement and drains exactly that many credits on summon (effect 'Hit[61,-cost,-cost,0]'). Range in the client data: 131 credits (Feeble Android) to 3694 credits (Ravening M-60, 275815). The eleven Automaton-line nanos (43325, 45692, 45710, 45704, 45718, 45724, 45737, 45676, 45731, 45698, 45681) carry NO cash requirement - the first bots are free.
petMechanics.controlThreshold: You must keep buffed Matter Creation and Time & Space at 80% of the nano's casting requirement or the bot goes over-equipped: it drops to behind/follow state and refuses every order ('Illegal command. Master not recognised.'). Over-equip percentage = 100 - (buffed skill / requirement) x 100; 20 or higher = over-equipped. Source: AO-Universe Over-Equipped guide + AODB Engineer:Tips and Tricks.
petMechanics.overEquipTrick: Cast the bot with a Trader Wrangle (and/or MP Mocham's Gift) up, then let the buff fade. Because control only needs 80% of the cast requirement, the bot keeps obeying. This is the core Engineer power curve at every bracket - AO-Universe's Engineer guide calls the difference between a self-cast bot and a Mocham's/Wrangle bot 'massive'.
petMechanics.range: Bots stop fighting and return to you beyond roughly 50 metres (AO-Universe Engineer Guide MKIII).
commands: /pet guard (default: follows, attacks anything that attacks you)
/pet wait (stops all action and clears its hate list - use this to hand aggro back in a team)
petMechanics.startupCrystal: Engineer: Startup Crystal - Feeble Automaton (item 43329) uploads nano 43325 'Feeble Automaton' (MC/TS 4, pet level 1). 'Engineer Robot Shell' (43328 / 46083) is the summoned shell item.
petMechanics._source: local: AOBuddy/GameData/profiles/engineer-nanos.json (from OmniCell Datafiles/nanos.ocp, names joined from itemnames.sql); Stat.cs Cash = 0x3D = 61.

botLadder.note: Complete robot ladder read from engineer-nanos.json category 'Pets - Robot' (90 of 90 nanos enumerated). 'pet' = the level of the summoned bot (2nd argument of SpawnItem). 'mc'/'ts' = the Matter Creation / Time & Space values in the cast action. 'cash' = credits drained on summon. Only the Shadowlands entries carry an explicit character-Level requirement; the whole Rubi-Ka ladder is gated by nano skill alone, which is exactly why wrangling works.

where: The Old Backyards (1-10) - reachable from Borealis / Newland City / West Athen / Rome
ICC Shuttleport / newbie island free-gear quests
brackets.fight: Rookie leets, rollerrats and the backyard grinder mobs. Do every free newbie quest for the NCU belt, backpack and starter tokens. Buy or roll the cheapest QL1-20 pistol or grenade launcher - your own damage barely matters yet.

Climb the free, cash-free Automaton line as fast as MC/TS allow: Feeble (43325, pet 1, MC/TS 4) -> Patchwork (45692, pet 2, 11) -> Lesser (45710, pet 3, 18) -> Inferior (45704, pet 4, 25) -> Flawed (45718, pet 5, 32) -> Common Automaton (45724, pet 6, 39). Leave the bot on /pet guard so it aggros for you. IP goes into Matter Creation and Time & Space above everything else.

where: Condemned Subway (8-20) - instanced; entrances in Borealis / West Athen / Rome Stretch; team BEFORE entering so you share one instance
RK newbie / team missions from mission terminals

where: Condemned Subway (8-20) - finish it and farm the Abmouth ring

froobVsPaid: FROOB (free play = Classic Rubi-Ka + free Notum Wars): hard level cap 200, NO Shadowlands, NO Alien Invasion, NO Lost Eden. For an Engineer this is a much softer cap than for most classes, and the reason is visible in the client data: the ENTIRE Rubi-Ka bot ladder up to Slayerdroid Guardian (45671, pet level 200, MC/TS 873, 1595 credits) carries NO Expansion requirement and NO character-level requirement - it is gated purely on Matter Creation and Time & Space. A twinked, wrangled froob Engineer can therefore run a level-200 bot well before level 200 and solo most of Rubi-Ka. Froob route: Arete / backyards -> Condemned Subway -> TOTW (must finish by 60) -> Virus Builders / Bot Hackers / Biomare -> Mort borgs -> PW borgs / The Reck / Smuggler's Den -> RK missions to 200. What froobs lose: the whole Shadowlands bot family (every Predator M-30 / Devastator Drone / Marauder M-45 / Desolator / Widowmaker nano carries Expansion BitAnd 2 plus a Specialization bit), the heckler/garden SK highway, levels 201-220, AI levels and perks, and LE research plus the Ofab Engineer set. PAID (SL) is the single biggest jump for an Engineer, because Specialization 2/3/4 are what unlock the top bots. PAID (AI) adds the AXP track and alien armor. PAID (LE) adds research, Battle Station VP and the Ofab Engineer set.
tips: The Engineer loop at EVERY level: summon the biggest bot you can control, /pet guard, send it, shoot from behind it, repair it, re-summon when it dies. Your own weapon is secondary until endgame.

WRANGLE THE BOT. Cast with a Trader Wrangle (and/or an MP's Mocham's Gift) running, then let the buff drop - you only need 80% of the cast requirement to keep control. AO-Universe's Engineer guide calls the difference between a self-cast bot and a Mocham's/Wrangle bot 'massive'. Every step of the ladder in this file is reachable a bracket early this way.

Watch the over-equip line: OE% = 100 - (buffed skill / requirement) x 100. At 20 or more the bot stops obeying, drops to behind/follow and answers 'Illegal command. Master not recognised.' Check /oe after every buff expiry and before a long fight.

CARRY CREDITS. Every bot from Feeble Android up literally spends credits to summon (a Cash stat-61 requirement plus a Hit[61,-cost] drain): 131 credits at pet level 17, 1595 at Slayerdroid Guardian, 3694 at Ravening M-60. Dying broke in a dungeon means no bot.
Matter Creation and Time & Space are the only two skills that drive your power curve, and they compete for the same implant slots - balance them rather than maxing one. Intelligence raises both.
Neleb's Nano-circuit Robe (151895) from TOTW is the classic Engineer MC/TS twink robe - farm it before level 60 and it carries you through many rungs of the bot ladder.

Run a team aura from the 60s on: the EngineerAuras strain 227 'Sympathetic ...' line (154550-154567) is a whole-team AC / reflect / damage-shield buff on its own nanoline, and it is a large part of why teams invite Engineers.

Learn /pet wait. It stops the bot and clears its hate list. An uncontrolled bot pulling extra mobs is the fastest way to be dropped from a team - AO-Universe: 'you generally cannot let it go on an uncontrolled rampage, it'll upset people in a team'.

Trim the bot: Positive Aggressive-Defensive (shop, QL100 max) lets you set its agg/def to 100%; Increase Aggressiveness (tradeskilled, QL200 max) raises its taunt by about 90 at QL200; Divert Energy to Offense (shop, QL200 max) gives roughly +40 AAO and +40 damage at the cost of 1000 AC and a 5-minute Mechanical Engineering lock.

Keep the Pet Heals line current (Quick Fix 116793 -> Patchy Repairs 116794 -> Recondition Parts 116797 -> Rebuild Casing 116792 -> Field Workshop 116796 -> Intricate Repairs 116795 -> A Maker's Touch 116791) and the Energize Shell / Conductive Spike line (203869 / 203871 / 203873 and 203861 / 203863 / 203865), which also strips the pet root and snare strains 145/146 - a rooted bot is a dead bot.
Cast the Jamming Tower (274369, nano crystal 274372) - it needs only MC/TS 19, so it is available at essentially any level and is a free deployable.

Beacon Warp (154914) and Team Beacon Warp (154913) are Engineer-only and Rubi-Ka-only (the nanos carry ExpansionPlayfield == 0). They warp a teamed, targeted player to you across zones and even into mission instances - the single most socially valuable utility an Engineer has for raids, mission runs and hauling a team to a camp.
Do TOTW boss loot BEFORE level 60 - the dungeon hard-locks entry past 60.
From 60 chase heckler teams; from 160 chase Adonis hecklers and Dark Ruins. Dark Ruins Solo (160-180) is especially good for an Engineer because the bot is a real tank.
Stack dailies once you own AI/LE: city dailies, Battle Station, alien daily / mothership and LE dailies give tokens, VP, AXP and XP in parallel.
Grind AI levels in city defense - the bot tanks alien attackers and your aura covers the defenders. Low risk, and you are useful while you farm.

Engineer is the tradeskill class (Mechanical Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Quantum Field Tech, Weapon Smithing, Nano Programming, Computer Literacy, Chemistry, Pharma Tech, Psychology, Breaking & Entering) and self-buffs most of it: EE 227652 / 227663, ME 227657 / 227667, QFT 227655 / 227665, Pharmaceuticals 227659 / 227669, Weapon Smithing 227661 / 227671, plus 'Engineer Composite Specialist Tradeskills (8 hours)' 273346 (+200 ME/EE/QFT). AO-Universe warns tradeskills eat all free IP before Title Level 6 - do not chase them before roughly level 125 if you want to level at pace.

Relative POWER of the Shadowlands bot families versus the Rubi-Ka families is NOT established. The data gives pet level, MC/TS and cost only. Note that 'Prototype Predator M-30' (223325) yields pet level 100 for MC/TS 687, while 'Perfected Guardbot' (45700) yields pet level 106 for MC/TS 553 - so the SL family is clearly not a simple linear upgrade. Test in game; do not assume a higher MC requirement means a better bot.
